```
### Java libraries (`lib/java/`, framework-agnostic)

The reusable Java library set (`dev.pathland`, Maven reactor, Java 17+) — the same
hand-written DSL serves Spring Boot, Quarkus, and desktop apps:

```
  `.modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(…).value(…)))`,
  `.modifiers(pathChange(p -> p.listener(…)))`), and the `*Mod` shims
  (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,
  `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed**.
- **Single-value shortcuts (spec DSL.md §2)**: a view/modifier whose config has a
  designated primary member also exposes a single-value construction overload that
  is pure sugar for the lambda — views construct with `make(value)` / `make(Signal<T>)`
  (`Text.make("hi")`), modifiers with the lowercase function's value form
  (`padding(16)`, `fontSize(sizeSignal)`). Multi-member configs (`Padding.edges`, `Offset`,
  `Gauge`, `Border`, …) have **no** shortcut — use the lambda. The shortcut delegates
  to the same `make(Consumer<Config>)` (views) / `Modifiers` facade
  (modifiers) factory via the package-private
  `Configurators` helper (one construction path). The former `.of(...)` construction
  factories are **removed** — a shortcut (or the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty
  `make()` for config-less views) replaces every one. Only data/branch factories keep
  `of`: `Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Case.of`, `Fit.of`, `EnvironmentKey.of`,
  `Route.of`, `Params.of`, `Signals.*`.
  Sizing is the `Frame` modifier value
  (`frame(f -> f.width(w).height(h).alignment(..))` and the lambda
  configurator `frame(f -> f.minWidth(..).maxWidth(..).alignment(..))`
  (min/ideal/max bounds)); all
  compile to the same `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT`/min-max `SET_PROPERTY`s.
  Typed enums
  (`Alignment`/`TextAlignment`/`FontWeight`/`Truncation`), not raw ints.
- **Environment scoping via a `ThreadLocal`** (Java 17+): a `ButtonStyle` modifier
  injects a style down the whole child tree; `ButtonStyle.makeBody(Configuration)`
  with built-in `PlainButtonStyle` / `BorderedButtonStyle`. Custom wrappers via
  `ViewModifier.body(View)`. The `Environment` also carries the session's
  `PersistentState`.
- **Reactivity (Angular parity)** in `com.pathland.view.signal`:
  `Signals.signal/computed/effect/untracked` — lazy+memoized computeds,
  glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression, error caching, write
  discipline (`allowWrites()`), circular-dependency detection.
- **Persisted view state** (`com.pathland.view.state`): a `State<T>` field (e.g.
  `State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);`) is auto-wired to the session's
  `PersistentState` (keyed by field name, or `new State<>(0, "key")` for an explicit
  key) by the `pathland-view-processor` annotation processor, which detects `State`
  fields by type and generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per view class. Each view
  connects its own `State` when it renders (`View.render` calls `Environment.state()
  → PersistentState.connect(view)`), so nested views can be instantiated inline in
  `body()` and need not be declared as fields. `PersistentState.signal(name, initial)`
  auto-loads the persisted value and auto-saves on change (key `name:scope`), and
  `StateStore` is untyped (one store serves all signal types).
- **Fine-grained emitter** (`com.pathland.view.emit`): mounts a view tree once,
  assigns stable ids, and registers a **node-level binding effect** per reactive
  text/property — a signal change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT` /
  `SET_PROPERTY` (unchanged signals emit zero opcodes). Sinks: `FrameOpcodeSink`
  (self-contained frames for SSR/WebSocket) and `RingOpcodeSink` (JNA into
  `libpathland_core`). The wire codec (`com.pathland.view.transport`) mirrors
  `pathland_core_transport` (`PLPL` batch format, self-contained frames + events).

Consistency with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the emitter/HTML
tests (golden byte layout + round-trips), replacing the old codegen assert pass.

- **Single signal value convention**: a view or modifier holds **one `Signal<T>`
  field** for a reactive value — never a raw field *plus* a signal field for the
  same value. Static values are authored through the raw config setter (or the
  `.of(T)` convenience), which
  wraps them in `Signals.constant(...)` (e.g. `Text.make(t -> t.text("Hello"))` ≡

  `ConstantSignal` as

  designated primary member also exposes a single-value construction overload that
  is pure sugar for the lambda — views construct with `make(value)` / `make(Signal<T>)`

  (`padding(16)`, `fontSize(sizeSignal)`). Multi-member configs (`Padding.edges`, `Offset`,
  `Gauge`, `Border`, …) have **no** shortcut — use the lambda. The shortcut delegates
  to the same `make(Consumer<Config>)` (views) / `Modifiers` facade
  (modifiers) factory via the package-private

  with built-in `PlainButtonStyle` / `BorderedButtonStyle`. Custom wrappers via

  glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression, error caching, write
  discipline (`allowWrites()`), circular-dependency detection.

  `PersistentState` (keyed by field name, or `new State<>(0, "key")` for an explicit

10:## Pathland is a protocol 35:## See it in action 55:## The flagship path today: SSR 86:## The whole app 133:## What it removes 141:## Why it's smooth 153:## The part you don't write 159:## Where it runs today 169:## Where it's headed 189:## Try it 242:## The technical details 252:## Status & license # Pathland > An open UI protocol. Declarative UI — written once in any language, rendered natively anywhere. **Status: proof of concept.** It works end to end and the tests are green, but the wire format and APIs may change before 1.0. [![CI](https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ## Pathland is a protocol Pathland is first and foremost a **binary UI protocol** — not just a framework, and not a single rendering target. Your view declaration compiles to fixed 16-byte opcodes that any renderer applies to native elements. The wire is the contract: a view written in Java, Rust, C#, or anything else produces the **same opcode stream**, and any renderer can apply it. That makes Pathland **language- and renderer-agnostic**: - **Write the UI once, declaratively.** A SwiftUI-shaped DSL in your language of choice — Java, Rust, C#, anything — describes the same view structure, whatever it later runs on. - **Run it on any surface.** The same view code drives today's server-rendered web and the native GTK4 desktop renderer, and is on track for the browser via WASM, embedded chips (LVGL), and native mobile/desktop (SwiftUI/UIKit, Jetpack Compose, Qt) ([Where it's headed](#where-its-headed)). - **Only changes travel.** The protocol is a stream of tiny binary deltas: an unchanged screen transmits zero bytes, and updates are applied in place. **Server-side rendering is the first surface we ship** — the flagship getting-started path — **not the whole story**. It's the on-ramp that's useful today; the protocol underneath is where the portability comes from. ## See it in action The same shared demo views, rendered by two of Pathland's surfaces — server-side HTML in the browser and native GTK4 widgets on the desktop:

Browser — SSR + live WebSocket deltas
Desktop — native GTK4 renderer
Try the hosted Quarkus demo live: **[pathland.onrender.com](https://pathland.onrender.com)**. ## The flagship path today: SSR The fastest way to replace a BFF + JavaScript-frontend stack. You write the **whole UI in your backend language** — Java, C#, Rust, anything. Pathland renders the first page as server-side HTML, so it appears instantly, then keeps it alive with tiny binary updates over a WebSocket. The result is a smooth, reactive UI — delivered by the backend team, without npm, bundlers, an extra build pipeline, or a separate frontend. ``` You declare the UI in your backend │ ▼ The server renders it (HTML) and owns it │ ▼ Only the things that change travel to the client │ ▼ The client applies them to native elements (60FPS) ``` - **You declare the UI** with a SwiftUI-shaped DSL — `VStack`, `Text`, `Button`, styling — right next to your business logic. - **The server renders and owns it.** The first page is plain HTML (instant paint, SEO-friendly); the server keeps the authoritative copy of the UI.

state.output:
Wherever it runs, only tiny binary updates travel across the ring buffer and are applied
in place — nothing is re-rendered or serialized, which is what keeps the UI stutter-free,
even on small devices.

## Try it

Each demo has a one-command launcher in [`scripts/`](./scripts/). Run one from the
repository root — it builds its own prerequisites (Rust dylibs, the Java reactor)
and launches:

| Script | Demo | What you get |
|--------|------|--------------|
| `./scripts/run-spring-demo.sh` | Spring Boot SSR + WebSocket | http://localhost:8080 |
| `./scripts/run-quarkus-demo.sh` | Quarkus SSR + WebSocket (hot reload) | http://localhost:8080 |
| `./scripts/run-rust-gtk-demo.sh` | Rust DSL → GTK4 desktop renderer | a native window |
| `./scripts/run-java-gtk-demo.sh` | Java DSL → GTK4 desktop renderer (the shared `SplitNavDemo`) | a native window |

```bash
# e.g. the Spring Boot demo
./scripts/run-spring-demo.sh
```

Notes:
- The web demos need a JDK 17+ (the whole stack runs on every LTS from 17).
- The GTK demos need the GTK4 + libadwaita system libraries.
- On macOS the Java GTK demo hands GTK the main thread automatically
  (`-XstartOnFirstThread`); Linux needs nothing special.

The same commands without the scripts:

```bash
# one-time: build the Rust HTML renderer (embedded in the jar), then the Java reactor
cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-render-html
cd lib/java && mvn install

# Spring Boot demo
cd lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo
mvn -q package && java -jar target/pathland-spring-boot-demo-0.1.0.jar
# → http://localhost:8080

# Quarkus demo (dev mode with hot reload)
cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo
mvn quarkus:dev
# → http://localhost:8080

# Same protocol, native GTK desktop renderer (no browser)
cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo

# Same protocol via Java: the shared demo views (SplitNavDemo) under the GTK renderer
cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk
cd lib/java/pathland-gtk-demo
MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread" mvn -q compile exec:java \
  -Dpathland.core.lib=$PWD/../../lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_core.dylib \
  -Dpathland.gtk.lib=$PWD/../../lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_gtk.dylib
# (macOS needs -XstartOnFirstThread; Linux can drop it)
```

## The technical details

This README is the *what*. The *how* — the wire protocol, the DSL contract, the
conformance vectors, and the implementation notes — lives in [`spec/`](./spec/):

- [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md) — the binary protocol
- [DSL.md](./spec/DSL.md) — the authoring surface (what you write)
- [PRIMITIVES.md](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md), [MODIFIERS.md](./spec/MODIFIERS.md), [EVENTS.md](./spec/EVENTS.md)
- [CONFORMANCE.md](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte vectors

## Status & license

Proof of concept. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md),
[CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md), and
[GENAI.md](./GENAI.md) (generative-AI transparency).
Licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('docs/typescript-view-plan.md')
s=p.read_text()
s=s.replace('**Status:** Approved — not started','**Status:** Implemented (phases 1–6); phase 7 is the next follow-up')
s=s.replace('| `TextField.text` | `BINDING_ID` 0x2017 + `VALUE` 0x2006 |','| `TextField.text` | `SET_TEXT` + `BINDING_ID` 0x2017 (matches the Rust/Java engines and DOM client) |')

s = before + sep + after
s += '''
---

## Phase 7 — Structural / conditional rendering (next)

Phase 1–6 keep the retained tree static after mount. The next phase adds
signal-selected structural slots:

- A slot declares a selector signal and a `() => ViewElement | null` content
  function.
- The engine reads the selector as a tracked dependency, re-evaluates the content
  untracked, and diffs the old/new subtree.
- Only `TREE` deltas are emitted (`CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`,
  `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD`); an identical recompute emits zero opcodes.
- Bindings and input routing for entering/leaving nodes are registered/destroyed
  with the subtree.
- Nested structural slots and stable ids where possible.

The wasm wrapper's output-buffer rule (copy before the next render) is already an
invariant of `@pathland/ssr/wasm.ts` and is covered by a consecutive-render test.
'''
p.write_text(s)

Now bigger concerns: is `@pathland/engine` `Emitter` re-export `InputDispatcher` okay? yes.

Need inspect server `express.ts`: SSR middleware `request.path.startsWith(`${base}/`)`; base `/_pathland`. If request path `/` works. If `/_pathland/ws` upgrade not through router. fine.

Need dynamic `route` update on `META::ENVIRONMENT` after mount: no re-render. Since phase 1 static. But when the client connects after SSR, live session created with env route from first message. Good. If environment arrives after session created (e.g. dispatch first), route set. Fine.

Need potential bug in `PathlandSession` constructor: `this.batcher` is created **after** `emitter.mount`. During mount, sink callback `handleFrame` stores initial frame; no batcher use. Good. But `this.initialFrame` assignment works even though `this.batcher` undefined? handleFrame only captures. Good.

Need potential bug in `PathlandSession` `renderHtml`: `this.options.ssrRenderer.renderDocument` uses `initialFrame`. If SSR session rendered after mount, okay. Live session renderHtml not used. Good.

Need potential bug in `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml`: if `store.load` returns `undefined`, `PathlandSession.create` sets `state ?? {}`; good.

Need potential bug in `PersistentState.state` save effect initial run: On `state()` creation, effect runs immediately and saves initial/loaded value. For SSR random scope, this writes defaults into MemoryStateStore under random scope (leak). Minor. Could avoid saving initial by comparing? Java does save initial too. Fine.

Need potential bug: `PathlandRegistry.close` enqueues close after other queue tasks. If an `environment` task is awaiting state load (slow Redis), close waits; okay but may mount then close. Fine.

Need potential bug: `PathlandRegistry.shutdown` doesn't close queues or wait. Fine for now.

Need potential bug: `DeltaBatcher.append` base calculation uses `this.strings.reduce` O(n^2), acceptable. It concatenates at flush.

Need verify string offset rebasing for `SET_TEXT` and `SET_PROPERTY` with frames from engine. Server test text delta works with one frame. Test batcher merging multiple frames? `resync` sends full. Could add a test for two text changes merged: set text twice before flush; opcodes both SET_TEXT rebased. Our `DeltaBatcher` parse/rebase each frame. Fine. Maybe add unit test with two frames to verify. Not necessary but risk. Let's add quick test in server test? It could catch offset bug. Use `BatchWriter` two frames with SET_TEXT "a","bb"; append both; flush; parse; read both. Add. Also sequence. Good.

Need check test imports `DeltaBatcher`, `BatchWriter`. Add. Let's add a small test.

state.output:
# pathland-ts-codegen — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 25, 2026

Generates the TypeScript DOM renderer's protocol-derived files from the canonical
Rust sources, so the TS side cannot drift silently.

## Implemented

- **`constants.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/constants.ts` and
  `packages/protocol/src/constants.ts`): every wire constant is
  bound to its `pathland_core::constants` source (a rename breaks compilation, a
  revalue changes the emitted file); the TypeScript server workspace gets the
  same bytes for its `@pathland/protocol` package. The protocol-semantic enum codes (alignment,
  shape kind, state, …) are enumerated from `spec/` — `ROLE_*` is bound to
  `pathland_core::constants::role` (the semantic-only catalog, dense 0–13) and
  `TEXT_STYLE_*` to `pathland_core::constants::text_style`.
- **`generated/tokens-core.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`):
  the design-token conventions (`tokenToCssVar`, `isDarkToken`,
  `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef` + length-token tables) emitted from
  `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the single source the Rust renderer and
  the DOM client share. `src/tokens.ts` imports it.
- **`generated/role-spec.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/role-spec.ts`):
  the semantic `ROLE` → element + typography → heading conventions emitted from
  `pathland_render_html::role_spec` — `ROLE_TAGS`, `HEADING_STYLES`,
  `ShellKind`, and the `semanticTag`/`textTag`/`ariaRole`/`headingLevel`
  resolvers — so semantic-tag / ARIA / heading decisions cannot drift between
  the Rust SSR renderer and the DOM client. `constants.ts` also carries the
  media surface (`COMPONENT_MEDIA_CONTROLLER`/`VIDEO`, `PROP_MEDIA_SOURCE`/
  `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`/`MEDIA_MUTED`/`MEDIA_LOOP`/`MEDIA_RATE`, and the
  `MEDIA_*` event commands) and the icon surface (`COMPONENT_ICON`,
  `PROP_ICON_NAME`).
- **Icon glyph map — intentionally NOT generated.** The full canonical icon
  catalog (`generated/icons.ts`, ~13KB in the bundle) was **removed**: the DOM
  client no longer carries glyph data. SSR inlines only the icons the page uses,
  and a runtime swap to a name the page did not embed lazily fetches
  `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from the host — which serves it from the shared
  Rust renderer (`pathland_html_icon_svg`, the same `pathland-render-html::icons`
  source SSR inlines from), so glyph parity between SSR and the client is
  guaranteed by the single Rust source, not by a mirrored TS map.
- **`npm run regen`** (`lib/typescript/scripts/regen.mjs`) runs both generators
  (`packages/protocol/src/constants.ts` is written by the same run)
  (and the golden-fixture emitter); CI's `rust` job runs them and fails on
  `git diff --exit-code` drift.

## Regenerate

`npm run regen` (from `lib/typescript`) or `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen`
(from `lib/rust`), then commit the generated files with the change that produced
them.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Only the pure-data surfaces are generated. The element-shell factory
  (`elements.ts`) and the property-handler table (`classes.ts`) are still
  hand-written — their alignment is enforced behaviorally by the
  `pathland-html-golden` conformance harness rather than generated. Extending
  the generator to those tables is the planned next step.

Index: .github/workflows/ci.yml
===================================================================
--- .github/workflows/ci.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/ci.yml	
@@ -1,256 +1,259 @@
 name: CI
 
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'spec/**']
   pull_request:
 
 jobs:
   rust:
     name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 
       # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
       # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
       # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
       # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
       # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
       # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
       # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
       # are installed in the next step.
       - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
         run: |
           sudo apt-get update
           sudo apt-get install -y \
             libgtk-4-dev \
             libadwaita-1-dev \
             libglib2.0-dev \
             libcairo2-dev \
             libpango1.0-dev \
             libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
             libgraphene-1.0-dev \
             libgstreamer1.0-dev \
             gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
             gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
             gstreamer1.0-libav
 
       - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
         run: |
           sudo apt-get install -y \
             qt6-base-dev \
             qt6-declarative-dev \
             qt6-declarative-private-dev \
             qt6-multimedia-dev \
             qml6-module-qtqml \
             qml6-module-qtqml-models \
             qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
             qml6-module-qtquick \
             qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
             qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
             qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
             qml6-module-qtquick-window \
             qml6-module-qtmultimedia
         # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
         # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
         # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
         # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
         # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
         # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.
 
       - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
         uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
         with:
           targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
 
       - name: Cache cargo
         uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
         with:
           workspaces: lib/rust -> target
 
       - name: Test workspace
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: cargo test
 
       - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
         working-directory: lib/rust
         env:
           QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
           QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
         run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

 # Pathland Project - AI Agent Guide
 
 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.
 
 **Last Updated**: October 22, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Java with the hand-written
 > **`com.pathland.view` DSL** (reusable library, Java 17+); both drive the engine
 > through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared
 > ring on desktop.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Java `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)

 language that links the dylib (Swift/Java/C# via FFI) calls the flat surface —
 no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.
 
 `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
 Java DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one

 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)

   with a wake closure.
 - Java demo (`pathland-gtk-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk` as a `cdylib` via JNA and
   calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Java DSL's own
   `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
   ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
   drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
   delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
   The demo mounts `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared views the web demos use) with the
   app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
   `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
   (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).

 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.

 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).

   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button`,
   `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, `Video` (a
   `MediaController`'s surface), and application code (Quarkus/Spring/desktop)
   defines its own views by implementing `View`. **Media is a state object, not a
   view** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` owns the resource + transport as
   signals, a `Video` surface renders it, and **audio has no view** — the app
   binds its own buttons/sliders (`controller.attach()` materializes the
   controller's node once, outside any swapping branch, so a band swap never
   restarts playback).

   app-authored `View` with values implements `Configurable<View.Config>`, holds a
   **`private` constructor**, and exposes
   `static ViewBuilder<View, Config> make(Consumer<Config>)`; a style
   (`ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`VideoStyle`) expose a
   **lowercase static factory** on their own type returning the style value
   (`BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(s -> s…)`), mirroring the library's
   `Modifiers.*` lowercase functions (e.g.
   `borderedButtonStyle(b -> b.padding(..).background(..)…)`). Creation goes
   through the configurator, never a parameterized constructor. The

   `pathland_core_transport` (`PLPL` batch format, self-contained frames + events).

   binding overhead. Controls' config fields for *distinct* properties
   (`min`/`max`/`step`/`placeholder`/`mode`/`style`) stay raw.
 
 ### TypeScript view + server (`packages/`, `examples/`)
 
 Angular-like TypeScript authoring plus a server-owned runtime. The browser keeps
 using the existing `@pathland/dom-renderer`; the server mounts the retained tree,
 emits PLPL snapshots/deltas, and renders SSR HTML through the Rust HTML renderer
 compiled to wasm. Rust remains the wire/SSR source of truth — not the TS runtime.
 
 ```
 packages/protocol/  # @pathland/protocol — generated constants, BatchWriter/Reader, EVENT/META decode
 packages/signals/   # @pathland/signals — callable signals, computed, effect, InputSignal
 packages/state/     # @pathland/state — StateStore, MemoryStateStore, State, PersistentState
 packages/view/      # @pathland/view — @view marker, elements, primitives, modifiers, AppContext
 packages/engine/    # @pathland/engine — retained tree, FrameOpcodeSink, Emitter, InputDispatcher
 packages/ssr/       # @pathland/ssr — wasm loader, page shell, bundle manifest
 packages/server/    # @pathland/server — sessions, registry, batcher, WebSocket, Express, Nest
 examples/profile-card/ # reference UserProfileCard + SSR/WS demo + Playwright e2e
+examples/music-player/ # TS MusicPlayerView (library/now-playing/player bar) + app-driven media + e2e
 ```
 
 - The pnpm workspace covers `packages/*` + `examples/*`. `lib/typescript` stays a
   separate npm package (the browser client).
 - `@view` is a legacy decorator marker; `body(props)` is called once per session.
 - Phase 1 is static-tree only: signals update text/properties, not structure.
   Structural/conditional reconciliation is the planned next phase.
+- Media: `MediaController` + `attach()` materialize a non-visual controller;
+  `Slider`/`Button`/`Icon` drive transport commands, and `MEDIA_*` reports feed
+  the controller signals. The music-player example is the reference.

   events write the bound `WritableSignal`.

   wrapper copies the bytes immediately.

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic

 ## Protocol Quick Reference
 
 The semantic surface is catalogued in the companion specs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`**
 (primitive views + component IDs), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (core modifiers = the

 **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract). The
 tables below are a quick recap of the protocol surface; the companion files

 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment |
 
 ### Component Types (u16)
 
 Grouped ranges (see `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`):
 
 | Group | Component | ID |
 |-------|-----------|----|
 | **Primitive Drawing (0x01–0x0F)** | TEXT | 0x01 |
 | | IMAGE | 0x02 |
 | | COLOR | 0x03 |
 | | SHAPE | 0x04 |
 | | DIVIDER | 0x05 |
 | | SPACER | 0x06 |
 | | PROGRESS_VIEW | 0x07 |
 | | GAUGE | 0x08 |
 | | VIDEO (a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER`'s surface) | 0x0A |
 | **Layout & Container (0x10–0x1F)** | VSTACK | 0x10 |
 | | HSTACK | 0x11 |
 | | ZSTACK | 0x12 |
 | | GRID | 0x13 |
 | | SCROLLVIEW | 0x14 |
 | | LAZY_VGRID | 0x15 |
 | | LAZY_HGRID | 0x16 |
 | | LAZY_VSTACK | 0x1B |
 | | LAZY_HSTACK | 0x1C |
 | **Semantic Control (0x20–0x2F)** | BUTTON | 0x20 |
 | | TEXT_FIELD (secure via `IS_SECURE`) | 0x21 |
 | | TEXT_EDITOR | 0x22 |
 | | TOGGLE (`TOGGLE_STYLE`: Switch/Checkbox/Button) | 0x24 |
 | | SLIDER | 0x25 |
 | | STEPPER | 0x26 |
 | | DATE_PICKER | 0x27 |
 | | PICKER | 0x28 |
 | | MENU | 0x29 |
 | | COLOR_PICKER | 0x2A |
 | **Media (0x30–0x3F)** | MEDIA_CONTROLLER (non-visual, owns playback) | 0x30 |
 | **Utility** | COMMENT | 0x7F |
 
 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005  
 **Text**: TEXT=0x000A, TEXT_ALIGNMENT=0x000C, LINE_LIMIT=0x000B, TRUNCATION_MODE=0x000D  
 **Style**: COLOR=0x100A, FONT_SIZE=0x1007, FONT_WEIGHT=0x1008, FONT_FAMILY=0x1009, BACKGROUND_COLOR=0x1001, BORDER_WIDTH=0x1003, BORDER_COLOR=0x1004, BORDER_RADIUS=0x1005, OPACITY=0x100D, VISIBLE=0x100E, Z_INDEX=0x100F, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=0x1010, PADDING=0x1011, PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT=0x1012-0x1015  
 **Special**: WIDTH=0x100B (use -1=FILL, -2=HUG_CONTENT), HEIGHT=0x100C  
 **Semantic**: ROLE=0x2001, STATE=0x2002, ENABLED=0x2003, SELECTED=0x2004, EVENT_LISTENERS=0x2005 (u32 bitmask — which raw events a node wants reported), VALUE=0x2006, MIN_VALUE=0x2007, MAX_VALUE=0x2008, LABEL=0x200A, PROMPT=0x200B  
 **Binding/action**: ACTION_ID=0x2016, BINDING_ID=0x2017, TOGGLE_STYLE=0x2018 (Switch=0, Checkbox=1, Button=2)  
 **Media** (spec/MEDIA.md): MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID=0x103A (a `VIDEO`'s controller), MEDIA_SOURCE=0x103B, MEDIA_MUTED=0x103C, MEDIA_LOOP=0x103D, MEDIA_RATE=0x103E; PLAYBACK_STATE=0x1035 / MEDIA_POSITION=0x1036 / MEDIA_VOLUME=0x1037 live on the controller
 
 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark), token resolution, effective color-scheme detection (platform-derived), interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`)
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 
 Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system) and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).

 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/`pathland-render-gtk` + tests
 4. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or
 renderer feature, a test that proves new surface — **update the affected
 project's `status.md`** (Implemented / Not implemented / gaps) in the same
 change. The specs (`spec/`) describe the protocol contract only and MUST NOT
 carry implementation status; status lives in `status.md` next to each
 implementing project.

 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |

 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)
 
 **When in doubt**: Check `spec/OPCODE.md`, the conformance vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, and the companion catalogs (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`), and the reference implementation (`pathland-core`). Ask: "Does this maintain stateless renderers?" "Does this only transmit actual changes?" "Does this describe WHAT the UI is, never WHERE?" "Is this representable as a 16-byte opcode in any language?"

You write the **whole UI in your backend language** — Java, C#, Rust, anything. Pathland renders the first page as server-side HTML, so it appears instantly, then keeps it alive with tiny binary updates over a WebSocket. The result is a smooth, reactive UI — delivered by the backend team, without npm, bundlers, an extra build pipeline, or a separate frontend. ``` You declare the UI in your backend │ ▼ The server renders it (HTML) and owns it │ ▼ Only the things that change travel to the client │ ▼ The client applies them to native elements (60FPS) ``` - **You declare the UI** with a SwiftUI-shaped DSL — `VStack`, `Text`, `Button`, styling — right next to your business logic. - **The server renders and owns it.** The first page is plain HTML (instant paint, SEO-friendly); the server keeps the authoritative copy of the UI. - **Only changes travel.** A click, a signal update, a navigation — the server sends a few tiny binary bytes describing exactly what changed. An unchanged screen sends nothing. The client applies them to real native elements (browser DOM, GTK widgets), so the platform does the layout, animation, and accessibility. ## The whole app Add one dependency and one bean, and you have a working app. **Spring Boot** ```java @SpringBootApplication public class MyApp { public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); } @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); } } ``` **Quarkus** ```java @ApplicationScoped public class MyApp implements PathlandApp { public View newRoot() { return new MyHomeView(); } } ``` `MyHomeView` is just Java views — the same code runs on both: ```java public final class MyHomeView implements View { State count = new State<>(0); // persisted per session, automatically @Override public View body() { return VStack.make(v -> v.alignment(HorizontalAlignment.CENTER).spacing(8)) .modifiers(padding(24)) .children( Text.make(Signals.computed(() -> "Clicked " + count.get() + " times")), Button.make(b -> b.title("Click me").action(() -> count.update(v -> v + 1)))); } } ``` That's it — SSR at any path, live updates over `/ws`, per-session state. *(Imports omitted: `com.pathland.server.PathlandApp`, `com.pathland.view.*`, and `import static com.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` for the modifier function.)* ## What it removes Today's server team pays for a BFF, a client-side state model, a SPA framework, and a JS build toolchain — all to render UI the server already owns. Pathland removes that layer: the backend *is* the application. There is no frontend contract to maintain, no client state model, and no JavaScript to write — and the same backend code that serves the web can drive other renderers later. ## Why it's smooth Pathland is built for smooth 60FPS UIs: - **Only changes are sent.** A screen that isn't changing transmits zero bytes. Updates are tiny binary deltas, not re-rendered pages or JSON trees. - **Native elements, not a canvas.** The platform lays out and animates real elements — you get native layout, text rendering, and accessibility for free, whether those elements are DOM nodes or GTK widgets. - **A thin client.** The web client is a small static file that hydrates the server HTML and applies updates in place. No framework, no virtual DOM, no re-render cost. ## The part you don't write The web client is a single prebuilt JavaScript file you copy into your static resources. It's shipped, not maintained — all the real logic lives in your backend. (There's also a native GTK renderer for desktop.) ## Where it runs today - **Web (SSR + live WebSocket deltas)** — Java, with Spring Boot and Quarkus starters and demos; the flagship getting-started path. - **Native desktop (GTK4)** — a renderer driven by the same protocol, from both the Rust DSL and the shared Java demo views (`pathland-gtk-demo`). Two surfaces, one protocol — the demos' shared views run under both without a rewrite. ## Where it's headed The SSR path above is the on-ramp — the protocol isn't limited to it. Write the app logic once, run it on embedded, mobile, desktop, and browser. Pathland is an open protocol, so the same code that drives the server-rendered UI today can also run on the device itself: - **In the browser**, the app logic compiles to WASM, writes to a shared buffer, and the main thread is left to rendering alone. - **On embedded devices**, the logic runs on one core while another core renders, with the ring buffer carrying the protocol between them — mapped onto a lightweight UI toolkit like LVGL. - **On mobile and desktop**, the same logic drives native renderers — SwiftUI/UIKit on Apple platforms, Jetpack Compose on Android, Qt and GTK on desktop. Wherever it runs, only tiny binary updates travel across the ring buffer and are applied in place — nothing is re-rendered or serialized, which is what keeps the UI stutter-free, even on small devices. ## Try it Each demo has a one-command launcher in [`scripts/`](./scripts/). Run one from the repository root — it builds its own prerequisites (Rust dylibs, the Java reactor) and launches: | Script | Demo | What you get | |--------|------|--------------| | `./scripts/run-spring-demo.sh` | Spring Boot SSR + WebSocket | http://localhost:8080 | | `./scripts/run-quarkus-demo.sh` | Quarkus SSR + WebSocket (hot reload) | http://localhost:8080 | | `./scripts/run-rust-gtk-demo.sh` | Rust DSL → GTK4 desktop renderer | a native window | | `./scripts/run-java-gtk-demo.sh` | Java DSL → GTK4 desktop renderer (the shared `SplitNavDemo`) | a native window | | `./scripts/run-profile-card-demo.sh` | TypeScript view DSL → wasm SSR + WebSocket | http://127.0.0.1:4317 | +| `./scripts/run-music-player-demo.sh` | TypeScript music player → app-driven media + deltas | http://127.0.0.1:4318 | ```bash # e.g. the Spring Boot demo ./scripts/run-spring-demo.sh ``` Notes: - The web demos need a JDK 17+ (the whole stack runs on every LTS from 17). - The GTK demos need the GTK4 + libadwaita system libraries. - On macOS the Java GTK demo hands GTK the main thread automatically (`-XstartOnFirstThread`); Linux needs nothing special. The same commands without the scripts: ```bash # one-time: build the Rust HTML renderer (embedded in the jar), then the Java reactor cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-render-html cd lib/java && mvn install # Spring Boot demo cd lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo mvn -q package && java -jar target/pathland-spring-boot-demo-0.1.0.jar # → http://localhost:8080 # Quarkus demo (dev mode with hot reload) cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo mvn quarkus:dev # → http://localhost:8080 # Same protocol, native GTK desktop renderer (no browser) cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo # Same protocol via Java: the shared demo views (SplitNavDemo) under the GTK renderer cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk cd lib/java/pathland-gtk-demo MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread" mvn -q compile exec:java \ -Dpathland.core.lib=$PWD/../../lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_core.dylib \ -Dpathland.gtk.lib=$PWD/../../lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_gtk.dylib # (macOS needs -XstartOnFirstThread; Linux can drop it) # TypeScript view DSL → server-owned runtime → wasm SSR + WebSocket deltas corepack pnpm install corepack pnpm build:wasm # Rust HTML renderer compiled to wasm corepack pnpm build:client # existing DOM hydration bundle corepack pnpm copy:client # content-hashed bundle into the example corepack pnpm --filter @pathland/example-profile-card start # → http://127.0.0.1:4317 + +# TypeScript music player: library + now-playing sidebar + app-driven audio +corepack pnpm --filter @pathland/example-music-player start +# → http://127.0.0.1:4318 ``` ## The technical details This README is the *what*. The *how* — the wire protocol, the DSL contract, the conformance vectors, and the implementation notes — lives in [`spec/`](./spec/): - [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md) — the binary protocol - [DSL.md](./spec/DSL.md) — the authoring surface (what you write) - [PRIMITIVES.md](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md), [MODIFIERS.md](./spec/MODIFIERS.md), [EVENTS.md](./spec/EVENTS.md) - [CONFORMANCE.md](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte vectors ## Status & license Proof of concept.  # Pathland TypeScript View + Server — Implementation Plan
 
 **Status:** Implemented (phases 1–6); phase 7 is the next follow-up
 **Scope:** TypeScript-only, server-driven UI
 **Last Updated:** October 22, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Goal
 
 Build a TypeScript authoring and server runtime for Pathland:
 
 - Angular-like developer experience: class views, decorators, callable signals,
   computed/effects, forced-once `body(props)`, fluent modifiers.
 - The application runs on the server. The server owns the retained tree,
   signals, state, and session lifecycle.
 - The browser hydrates SSR HTML and applies deltas. It does **not** run the
   view engine in this phase.
 - SSR is rendered by the existing Rust `pathland-render-html` crate compiled to
   WebAssembly.
 - The browser client is the existing `lib/typescript` `@pathland/dom-renderer`.
 - Rust remains the source of truth for wire constants/conformance and the HTML
   renderer. Rust is not the runtime engine.
 
 ## Locked decisions
 
 | Decision | Choice |
 |---|---|
 | Language | TypeScript only |
 | AssemblyScript | Out of scope; no `view-as`, no closure transform, no dual-target |
 | DX | Angular-like: class views, `@view`, callable signals, `body(props)`, modifiers |
 | View restrictions | None from AS: optional props, closures, unions, and full TS are allowed |
 | Execution model | Server-owned app; browser is a renderer |
 | Browser runtime | Deferred; same TS engine must stay worker-compatible later |
 | SSR | Rust `pathland-render-html` via a small wasm wrapper |
 | Client | Reuse `lib/typescript` `@pathland/dom-renderer` |
 | Server host | Node first; framework-agnostic core; Bun/Deno later |
 | State | In-memory now; Redis interface documented and deferred |
 | Context | Small `AppContext` (state/platform/route); no full Angular DI |
 | Structural reactivity | Later; the reference view is static |
 | Wire format | Existing 16-byte opcodes + PLPL batches, protocol v1 |
 
 ### Why not the alternatives
 
 - **AssemblyScript / wasm app runtime:** rejected for this phase. It forces an
   AS-native DSL and a closure transform, sacrificing the Angular-like DX.
 - **Rust engine runtime:** rejected. A TS app on Node would need per-call FFI;
   a non-Node host would need an embedded JS runtime. The TS engine is the future
   browser/worker runtime anyway.
 - **A separate TS HTML serializer:** rejected as the primary path. Reuse the
   Rust HTML renderer for parity with the existing renderers.
 
 ## Non-goals
 
 - No AssemblyScript compiler, transform, or runtime.
 - No TS/AS byte-identity work.
 - No SharedArrayBuffer ring, transferable double buffering, or worker DOM
   patcher.
 - No browser-side application runtime in this phase.
 - No Rust `pathland-engine` runtime dependency.
 - No full Angular DI container, router, or zone.js.
 - No structural/conditional rendering in phase 1; plan it as a follow-up.
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ```text
 TypeScript view + engine (server)
         │
         ├── PLPL snapshot / delta batches
         │        ├── Rust pathland-render-html (WASM) → SSR HTML
         │        └── WebSocket → existing @pathland/dom-renderer
         │
         └── raw EVENT batches ← WebSocket ← browser
 ```
 
 ### Server flow
 
 1. **SSR request**
    - Create a throwaway session with a random state scope.
    - Instantiate the app, connect state, mount the root view once.
    - Emit a full snapshot batch.
    - Render it with the Rust HTML wasm renderer.
    - Inject `data-pathland-base` and the content-hashed client bundle.
    - Close the throwaway session.
 2. **WebSocket connect**
    - Client URL: `<base>/ws?wid=<window-id>`.
    - Register a pending session. The first message is `META::ENVIRONMENT`.
    - Create the live session with the `wid` state scope.
    - Do not re-send the mount frame; the client already has the SSR HTML.
 3. **Deltas**
    - Signal changes emit only the affected opcodes.
    - Send monotonic PLPL batches when the connection is open.
    - `META::RESYNC` re-emits the full tree.
    - `META::PING` → `META::PONG`.
 4. **Events**
    - Client sends raw EVENT batches.
    - The server updates bound signals; the engine emits deltas.
 5. **Persistence**
    - Load `StateStore` values before mount.
    - Save on `State` changes.
    - Memory store now; Redis later.
 
 ---
 
 ## Repository layout
 
 ```text
 pnpm-workspace.yaml
 package.json
 tsconfig.base.json
 
 packages/
 ├── protocol/     @pathland/protocol
 ├── signals/      @pathland/signals
 ├── state/        @pathland/state
 ├── view/         @pathland/view
 ├── engine/       @pathland/engine
 ├── ssr/          @pathland/ssr
 └── server/       @pathland/server
 
 examples/
-└── profile-card/
+├── profile-card/
+└── music-player/
 
 lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html-wasm/   # new wasm wrapper
 ```
 
 The existing `lib/typescript` package remains the browser client. It is not
 converted to a pnpm workspace member in this phase.
 
 ### Package dependency direction
 
 ```text
 protocol
 signals
   └── state
         └── view
               └── engine
                     └── server
-                          └── examples/profile-card
+                          ├── examples/profile-card
+                          └── examples/music-player

   └── ssr
 ```
 
 No circular dependencies. `engine` imports neither DOM nor Node APIs.
 
 ---
 
 ## Package contracts
 
 ### `@pathland/protocol`
 
 ```text
 packages/protocol/src/
   constants.ts   # generated from Rust pathland-ts-codegen
   batch.ts       # PLPL BatchWriter / BatchReader
   events.ts      # EVENT + META decode
   index.ts
 ```
 
 ```ts
 export interface Opcode {
   category: number;
   command: number;
   flags: number;
   a: number;
   b: number;
   c: number;
 }
 
 export class BatchWriter {
   begin(): void;
   push(category: number, command: number, flags: number, a: number, b: number, c: number): void;
   string(value: string): number;  // arena offset
   end(sequence: number): Uint8Array;
 }
 
 export interface EventOpcode extends Opcode {
   text?: string;
 }
 
 export function decodeEvents(bytes: Uint8Array): EventOpcode[];
 ```
 
 - Reuse the PLPL header/opcode/string layout already parsed by
   `lib/typescript/src/plpl.ts`.
 - Use the existing implementation packing:
   `B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId`.
 - F32 values are stored as raw IEEE-754 bits.
 - Strings are length-prefixed UTF-8 in the batch string section.
 
 ### `@pathland/signals`
 
 ```text
 packages/signals/src/
   signal.ts
   computed.ts
   effect.ts
   input.ts
   index.ts
 ```
 
 ```ts
 export interface ReadonlySignal<T> {
   (): T;
   get(): T;
 }
 
 export interface WritableSignal<T> extends ReadonlySignal<T> {
   set(value: T): void;
   update(fn: (current: T) => T): void;
 }
 
 export type MaybeSignal<T> = T | ReadonlySignal<T>;
 
 export class InputSignal {
   static from<T>(
     value: MaybeSignal<T> | null | undefined,
     fallback?: T,
   ): ReadonlySignal<T>;
 }
 ```
 
 - Callable signals, Angular-style.
 - Lazy memoized `computed`, synchronous `effect` flush, equality suppression,
   error caching, cleanup handles.
 - `InputSignal.from` wraps raw values in a constant signal; existing signals
   pass through.
 - The reference view's optional `status` and closure syntax are fully allowed.
 
 ### `@pathland/state`
 
 ```text
 packages/state/src/
   store.ts
   state.ts
   index.ts
 ```
 
 ```ts
 export interface StateStore {
   load(scope: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> | Record<string, unknown>;
   save(scope: string, key: string, value: unknown): void | Promise<void>;
   delete(scope: string, key: string): void | Promise<void>;
 }
 
 export class MemoryStateStore implements StateStore {}
 
 export class State<T> {
   readonly key: string;
   readonly signal: WritableSignal<T>;
 }
 
 export class PersistentState {
   connect(target: object): void; // binds State<T> fields by property name
   state<T>(key: string, initial: T): WritableSignal<T>;
 }
 ```
 
 - `State<T>` fields are auto-connected by property name when
   `PersistentState.connect` runs before mount.
 - The loaded value wins over the initializer.
 - Writes save through the store; the key is scoped by the session.
 - Redis is not implemented now; see [State and Redis](#state-and-redis).
 
 ### `@pathland/view`
 
 ```text
 packages/view/src/
   decorator.ts    # @view marker
   element.ts      # ViewElement model
   primitives.ts   # VStack/HStack/ZStack/Text/Image/TextField/Button
   modifiers.ts    # padding/cornerRadius/background/fontSize/foregroundStyle
   context.ts      # AppContext + useAppContext()
   index.ts
 ```
 
 ```ts
 export function view<T extends object>(target: T): T;
 
 export type ViewChildren = ViewElement[] | (() => ViewElement[]);
 
 export function VStack(props: VStackProps, children: ViewChildren): ViewElement;
 export function HStack(props: HStackProps, children: ViewChildren): ViewElement;
 export function Text(props: TextProps): ViewElement;
 export function Image(props: ImageProps): ViewElement;
 export function TextField(props: TextFieldProps): ViewElement;
 export function Button(props: ButtonProps): ViewElement;
 
 export interface Element {
   modifiers(...mods: ViewModifier[]): ViewElement;
 }
 
 export function useAppContext(): AppContext;
 ```
 
 - `@view` is a legacy TypeScript decorator marker; mounting is explicit.
 - `body(props)` is called once per session.
 - Children functions are evaluated once during mount.
 - `AppContext` is available synchronously during `body`/mount via a stack.
 - `AppContext` contains `state`, `platform`, and `route`; no full injector.
 
 ### `@pathland/engine`
 
 ```text
 packages/engine/src/
   node.ts       # retained node types
   sink.ts       # FrameOpcodeSink backed by BatchWriter
   bindings.ts   # text/property bindings + effect cleanup
   emitter.ts    # mount / snapshot / delta / destroy
   input.ts      # RenderResult + InputDispatcher
   index.ts
 ```
 
 ```ts
 export interface RenderResult {
   rootId: number;
   textInputs: Map<number, WritableSignal<string>>;
   valueInputs: Map<number, WritableSignal<number>>;
   tapActions: Map<number, () => void>;
 }
 
 export class Emitter {
   mount(root: ViewElement, ctx: AppContext): RenderResult;
   renderFull(): void;
   destroy(): void;
 }
 
 export class InputDispatcher {
   constructor(result: RenderResult, route: WritableSignal<string>);
   dispatch(events: EventOpcode[]): void;
 }
 ```
 
 Behavior:
 
 - Deterministic node IDs in pre-order, starting at 1.
 - Initial mount emits the full tree.
 - Signal changes emit only `SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`.
 - An unchanged signal emits zero opcodes.
 - `TextField` binds a `WritableSignal<string>` and registers in
   `RenderResult.textInputs`.
 - `Button`/tap handlers register in `tapActions`.
 - No structural re-evaluation in phase 1.
 - Canonical emission order:
   1. `CREATE_NODE`
   2. config properties
   3. modifiers in source order
   4. text content
   5. each child subtree, then `INSERT_CHILD`
 
 Property mapping for the reference:
 
 | DSL | Protocol |
 |---|---|
 | `VStack` | `VSTACK` (0x10) |
 | `HStack` | `HSTACK` (0x11) |
 | `Text` | `TEXT` (0x01) |
 | `Image` | `IMAGE` (0x02) |
 | `TextField` | `TEXT_FIELD` (0x21) |
 | `spacing` | `SPACING` 0x0001, F32 |
 | `alignment` | `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002, F32 enum |
 | `padding` | `PADDING` 0x1011, F32 |
 | `cornerRadius` | `BORDER_RADIUS` 0x1005, F32 |
 | `background` | `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001, COLOR |
 | `fontSize` | `FONT_SIZE` 0x1007, F32 |
 | `foregroundStyle` | `COLOR` 0x100A, COLOR |
 | `Image.source` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` 0x1002, STRING |
 | `Text.text` | `SET_TEXT`, arena ref |
 | `TextField.placeholder` | `PROMPT` 0x200B, STRING |
 | `TextField.text` | `SET_TEXT` + `BINDING_ID` 0x2017 (matches the Rust/Java engines and DOM client) |
 
 ### `@pathland/ssr`
 
 ```text
 packages/ssr/src/
   wasm.ts
   page.ts
   assets.ts
   index.ts
 ```
 
 ```ts

   renderDocument(batch: Uint8Array, rootId: number): string;
   renderFragment(batch: Uint8Array, rootId: number): string;

   base: string;
 ```

 ### `@pathland/server`
 
 ```text
 packages/server/src/
   app.ts
   connection.ts
   session.ts
   registry.ts
   batcher.ts
   queue.ts
   ws.ts
   express.ts
   nest.ts
   index.ts
 ```
 
 ```ts
 export interface PathlandApp {
   newRoot(ctx: AppContext): ViewElement;
 }
 
 export interface PathlandConnection {
   send(bytes: Uint8Array): void;
   isOpen(): boolean;
 }
 
 export class PathlandSession {
   constructor(options: {
     sessionId: string;
     app: PathlandApp;
     store: StateStore;

   });

   dispatch(uiId: string, bytes: Uint8Array): void;
 ```

 Port the behavior of the Java server core:
 
 - `lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandSession.java`
 - `PathlandRegistry.java`
 - `PathlandAssets.java`
 - `PathlandConnection.java`
 
 Important semantics:
 
 - The mount frame is emitted in the session constructor but not sent.
 - Live deltas are sent only after `connect`.
 - `resync()` re-emits the full tree.
 - Sessions are created lazily on the first `META::ENVIRONMENT`.
 - The SSR path uses a throwaway session with a random scope.
 - The live session uses the client's `wid` scope.
 - Per-session operations are serialized with a queue; signals remain
   single-threaded.
 
 ---
 
 ## Rust changes
 
 Add:
 
 ```text
 lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html-wasm/
 ```
 
 - Depends on `pathland-render-html` and `pathland-core-transport`.
 - `publish = false`.
 - `crate-type = ["cdylib"]`.
 - Exports:
 
 ```rust
 pathland_wasm_alloc(len: u32) -> *mut u8
 pathland_wasm_free(ptr: *mut u8, len: u32)
 pathland_wasm_render(
   batch: *const u8,
   len: u32,
   root: u32,
   fragment: u8,
   out_len: *mut u32,
 ) -> *const u8
 ```
 
 - Reuse `decode_frame` and `HtmlRenderer::render_document/render_fragment`.
 - Build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
 - Copy the output to `packages/ssr/wasm/pathland_render_html.wasm`.
 - Add a build script and CI step.
 - Add a TS wasm smoke test.
 
 Also extend `pathland-ts-codegen` to emit
 `packages/protocol/src/constants.ts`, and include it in the existing no-drift
 CI check.
 
 No wire-format changes.
 
 ---
 
 ## SSR and hydration
 
 - The Rust renderer returns a complete HTML document.
 - `renderPage` injects:
   - `data-pathland-base="<base>"` on `<html>`;
   - `<script src="<base>/<bundleName>" defer></script>` before `</body>`.
 - Phase 1 omits the service worker; add it later.
 - Reuse the existing client bundle:
   `lib/typescript/dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js`.
 - Add a copy script that writes a content-hashed bundle and a
   `dom-renderer.current` manifest into the example's static asset directory.
 - The server resolves the current bundle name from the manifest.
 - Client behavior already provided by `lib/typescript`:
   - hydrate `data-pathland-id` nodes;
   - `wid` in `sessionStorage`, sent only on the WS URL;
   - `META::ENVIRONMENT` as the first WS message;
   - `META::RESYNC` on reload/reconnect;
   - heartbeat `META::PING`/`PONG`;
   - sequence-gap detection;
   - raw event batches.
 
 The server must implement those META messages and the sequence numbering.
 
 ---
 
 ## State and Redis
 
 Phase 1:
 
 - `MemoryStateStore`.
 - `PersistentState` loads before mount and saves on change.
 - Scope: `"/" + wid` for the root app; mount-qualified for multi-app later.
 
 Redis (deferred, documented now):
 
 - Package: `@pathland/state-redis`.
 - Keys: `pathland:<mount>:<wid>:<state-key>`.
 - Values: JSON or a typed encoding.
 - `StateStore.load` is awaited before the live session mount.
 - The SSR throwaway session does not load persisted state unless a `wid` is
   supplied.
 - Document TTL, serialization, and failure behavior.
 
 ---
 
 ## Testing
 
 ### Unit
 
 - `protocol`: batch writer/reader round-trip, known bytes, event decode,
   generated constants no-drift.
 - `signals`: callable reads, dependency tracking, equality, computed
   memoization, synchronous effects, cleanup.
 - `state`: memory store, scope keys, load-before-mount, save-on-change.
 - `engine`: node IDs, property order, text binding, zero-op unchanged update,
   snapshot vs delta.
 - `ssr`: wasm load, document/fragment render, escaped text, `data-pathland-id`.
 
 ### Integration
 
 - Express SSR response contains the expected HTML, base, and script.
 - WS connect sends `META::ENVIRONMENT`; the session is created with the `wid`
   scope.
 - `META::RESYNC` returns a full snapshot.
 - `TEXT_CHANGED` updates the `TextField` signal and emits the expected delta.
 - `META::PING` receives `META::PONG`.
 - Sequence numbers are monotonic.
 
 ### End-to-end
 
 - Playwright against `examples/profile-card`:
   - load SSR HTML;
   - hydrate;
   - type into the `TextField`;
   - server updates the bound signal;
   - a `Text` echo updates via delta;
   - no full-tree re-emit on each keystroke.

   - pnpm install;
   - build/typecheck/test all packages;

   - build the existing `lib/typescript` client bundle;

 - Existing Rust job:
   - build/test the wasm wrapper natively;
   - upload the wasm artifact for the TS job.

 ## Acceptance criteria
 
 1. `UserProfileCard.ts` compiles with only `public` → `export` changed.
 2. `pnpm -r typecheck` and `pnpm -r test` pass.
 3. SSR returns the reference card with:
    - `data-pathland-id` nodes;
    - avatar image;
    - username/status text;
    - search input;
    - background, radius, padding, font sizes, colors.
 4. The browser hydrates the SSR DOM without duplicating nodes.
 5. Typing in the search input updates the server-side writable signal.
 6. The server emits a delta; the DOM updates without a full tree re-emit.
 7. Reloading the same tab requests `META::RESYNC` and restores the session
    state.
 8. `META::PING` gets `META::PONG`.
 9. The Rust HTML renderer is used for SSR; no TS HTML serializer is required.
 10. No AssemblyScript artifacts or dependencies.

 ## Reference view
 
 The only required source change is the invalid top-level `public` modifier:
 
 ```diff
 -public interface UserProfileCardProps {
 +export interface UserProfileCardProps {
 ```
 
 Full reference (unchanged otherwise):
 
 ```ts
 import { view, InputSignal } from "@pathland/view";
 import { Text, Image, HStack, VStack, TextField } from "@pathland/view/primitives";
 import { padding, cornerRadius, background, fontSize, foregroundStyle } from "@pathland/view/modifiers";
 import { MaybeSignal, WritableSignal } from "@pathland/signals";
 
 export interface UserProfileCardProps {
   username: MaybeSignal<string>;
   status?: MaybeSignal<string>;
   searchQuery: WritableSignal<string>;
 }
 
 @view
 export class UserProfileCard {
   body(props: UserProfileCardProps) {
     const usernameSignal = InputSignal.from(props.username);
     const statusSignal = InputSignal.from(props.status, "Offline");
 
     return VStack({ spacing: 12 }, () => [
       HStack({ spacing: 16 }, () => [
         Image({ source: "avatar.png" }).modifiers(
           cornerRadius(24),
           padding(4),
         ),
 
         VStack({ alignment: "leading", spacing: 4 }, () => [
           Text({ text: usernameSignal }).modifiers(
             fontSize(18),
             foregroundStyle("#111827"),
           ),
 
           Text({ text: statusSignal }).modifiers(
             fontSize(12),
             foregroundStyle("#10B981"),
           ),
         ]),
       ]),
 
       TextField({
         placeholder: "Search user...",
         text: props.searchQuery,
       }),
     ]).modifiers(
       background("#FFFFFF"),
       cornerRadius(12),
       padding(16),
     );
   }
 }
 ```
 
 ---
 
 ## Risks and notes
 
 - **Rust wasm wrapper:** keep the ABI small and test it from Node; avoid
   caching `memory.buffer` across renders.
 - **Client protocol details:** `wid`, `RESYNC`, `PING`/`PONG`, and sequence
   numbers are already implemented by `lib/typescript`; port the Java server
   behavior exactly.
 - **Duplicate PLPL codec:** the server and client each have a codec. Add
   cross-tests; consolidate later if practical.
 - **Async state:** Redis will make session creation asynchronous. The
   per-session queue must hold environment/events until mount completes.
 - **Session lifecycle:** add a TTL/idle cleanup to avoid leaking server-side
   trees and signals.
 - **Static tree only:** conditional rendering and structural reconciliation
   are follow-ups. Warn against relying on state-dependent structure in SSR
   until RESYNC/reconcile is fully tested.
 - **Determinism:** use `AppContext.platform.now()`/random when SSR and the live
   session must agree; avoid direct `Date.now()`/`Math.random()` in `body`.
 - **No AS:** do not introduce `view-as`, `asconfig`, the closure transform, or
   AS-compatible view restrictions.
 - **No Rust engine runtime:** do not add a native addon or per-opcode FFI.
 
 ---
 
 ## Phase 7 — Structural / conditional rendering (next)
 
 Phase 1–6 keep the retained tree static after mount. The next phase adds
 signal-selected structural slots:
 
 - A slot declares a selector signal and a `() => ViewElement | null` content
   function.
 - The engine reads the selector as a tracked dependency, re-evaluates the content
   untracked, and diffs the old/new subtree.
 - Only `TREE` deltas are emitted (`CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`,
   `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD`); an identical recompute emits zero opcodes.
 - Bindings and input routing for entering/leaving nodes are registered/destroyed
   with the subtree.
 - Nested structural slots and stable ids where possible.
 
 The wasm wrapper's output-buffer rule (copy before the next render) is already an
 invariant of `@pathland/ssr/wasm.ts` and is covered by a consecutive-render test.

+    width(280),

+    background(SIDEBAR_BG),
+  );
+}
+
+function UpNextRow(state: PlayerBindings, offset: number): ViewElement {
+  return Text({
+    text: computed(() => {
+      const track = at(state.trackIndex() + offset);
+      return `${offset === 1 ? "Up next" : "Then"} · ${track.title} — ${track.artist}`;
+    }),
+  }).modifiers(fontSize(13), foregroundStyle(SECONDARY_FG), lineLimit(1));
+}
+
+function PlayerBar(
+  state: PlayerBindings,
+  current: ReadonlySignal<Track>,
+): ViewElement {
+  const seek = seekValue(state.player.time, state.player.position);
+  const volume = volumeValue(state.player.volumeReport, state.player.volume);
+  const transportIcon = computed(() => (state.playing() ? "pause" : "play"));
+  const progress = computed(
+    () =>
+      `${fmt(state.player.time())} / ${fmt(
+        state.player.duration() > 0 ? state.player.duration() : current().duration,
+      )}`,
+  );
+
+  const transport = HStack({ spacing: 14, alignment: "center" }, () => [
+    iconButton("skip-back", state.prev),
+    iconButton(transportIcon, state.player.toggle.bind(state.player)),
+    iconButton("skip-forward", state.next),
+  ]);
+
+  const trackInfo = HStack({ spacing: 12, alignment: "center" }, () => [
+    Image({ source: computed(() => current().cover) }).modifiers(
+      width(36),
+      height(36),
+      scaledToFit(),
+      cornerRadius(4),
+    ),
+    VStack({ spacing: 2, alignment: "leading" }, () => [
+      Text({ text: computed(() => current().title) }).modifiers(
+        fontWeight(600),
+        lineLimit(1),
+        width(160),
+      ),
+      Text({ text: computed(() => current().artist) }).modifiers(
+        fontSize(13),
+        foregroundStyle(SECONDARY_FG),
+        lineLimit(1),
+        width(160),
+      ),
+    ]),
+  ]);
+
+  const volumeControl = HStack({ spacing: 10, alignment: "center" }, () => [
+    Icon({ name: "volume" }).modifiers(fontSize(16)),
+    Slider({ value: volume, min: 0, max: 1 }).modifiers(width(110)),
+  ]);
+
+  return VStack({ spacing: 2 }, () => [
+    HStack({ spacing: 18, alignment: "center" }, () => [
+      transport,
+      Text({ text: "|" }).modifiers(fontSize(18), foregroundStyle(SECONDARY_FG)),
+      trackInfo,
+      Spacer(),
+      Text({ text: progress }).modifiers(fontSize(12), foregroundStyle(SECONDARY_FG)),
+      volumeControl,
+    ]).modifiers(fillWidth()),
+    Slider({ value: seek, min: 0, max: 100 }).modifiers(fillWidth()),
+  ]).modifiers(
+    padding(12),
+    fillWidth(),
+    height(76),
+    background(BAR_BG),
+  );
+}
+
+function iconButton(icon: ReadonlySignal<string> | string, action: () => void): ViewElement {
+  return Button({
+    action,
+    children: () => [Icon({ name: icon }).modifiers(fontSize(18))],
+  }).modifiers(padding(6));
+}
+
+/** The seek slider: displays `time`, writes both `time` (feedback) and `position` (command). */
+function seekValue(
+  time: WritableSignal<number>,
+  position: WritableSignal<number>,
+): WritableSignal<number> {
+  return writableAdapter(
+    () => time(),
+    (value) => {
+      time.set(value);
+      position.set(value);
+    },
+  );
+}
+
+/** The volume slider: displays `volumeReport`, writes both report and command. */
+function volumeValue(
+  report: WritableSignal<number>,
+  volume: WritableSignal<number>,
+): WritableSignal<number> {
+  return writableAdapter(
+    () => report(),
+    (value) => {
+      report.set(value);
+      volume.set(value);
+    },
+  );
+}
+
+function writableAdapter(read: () => number, write: (value: number) => void): WritableSignal<number> {
+  const callable = (() => read()) as WritableSignal<number>;
+  return Object.assign(callable, {
+    get: read,
+    set: write,
+    update: (fn: (current: number) => number) => write(fn(read())),
+    __pathlandSignal: true as const,
+    __pathlandWritable: true as const,
+  });
+}
+
+export { SECONDARY_FG };

+/** The track at an index (wraps around, safe for negative indexes). */
+export function at(index: number): Track {
+  const length = TRACKS.length;

+  const total = Math.max(0, Math.round(seconds));

+# examples/music-player — status
+
+**Last updated:** October 22, 2026
+
+## Implemented
+
+- Apple Music-style player authored with the TypeScript view DSL:
+  - library list with selectable rows and reactive active-row highlighting;
+  - now-playing sidebar with reactive album art/title/artist and up-next rows;
+  - player bar with prev/play-pause/next, track info, progress, seek, and volume.
+- App-owned persisted transport state (`player.track`, `player.playing`,
+  `player.position`, `player.volume`, seek/volume commands).
+- `MediaController` bound to the app signals; actual audio plays through the
+  existing DOM client's media pipeline (`MEDIA_*` commands + reports).
+- Reuses the shared Java demo's album art/audio assets under
+  `/_pathland/assets/`.
+- Playwright e2e: SSR content, track selection (source/cover/title deltas),
+  play/pause icon toggling, and live range inputs.
+
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- Karaoke lyric pill and the sponsored proxy slot from the Java demo are not
+  ported.
+- Seek is live rather than seek-on-release; no `EDITING_CHANGED` deferral.
+- The demo uses `MemoryStateStore` (no Redis persistence).

 # @pathland/engine — status
 
 **Last updated:** October 22, 2026
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - Deterministic pre-order node ids starting at 1.
 - Retained tree + `FrameOpcodeSink` over `BatchWriter`.
 - Canonical emission order: create, config properties, modifiers, binding id,
   text, child subtree + insert.
-- Text/property binding effects; unchanged signals emit zero opcodes.
+- Text/property binding effects (including reactive string/color/number
+  properties and `MEDIA_*` controller properties); unchanged signals emit zero
+  opcodes.
 - `renderFull()` for resync.
 - `RenderResult` + `InputDispatcher` for taps, text/value changes, and
   navigation.
-- `TextField` binds `SET_TEXT` + `BINDING_ID`; `Button` emits pointer listener
-  bits and routes taps.
+- `TextField` binds `SET_TEXT` + `BINDING_ID`; `Slider` binds `VALUE` and routes
+  value events; `Button` emits pointer listener bits and routes taps.
+- `MediaController` materialization: one `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node with source,
+  playback state, position, volume, mute, loop, rate; `MEDIA_*` reports route to
+  the controller.
 - Tests cover snapshot opcodes, delta-only updates, zero-op unchanged writes,
   full re-emit, text input routing, and button taps.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - No structural reconciliation (`CREATE`/`DELETE`/`INSERT`/`MOVE` for dynamic
   subtrees); the retained tree is static after mount.
-- Value-control bindings are represented in `RenderResult` but not emitted by a
-  primitive yet.
+- `VIDEO` surfaces and size-that-fits slots are not implemented.
